messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

It’s mostly fine, though I’d rather the trailer weren’t taking up space on my pad; I could use the room and it would feel less like something I have to work around. I did agree to the arrangement, so I feel a bit bad wanting it gone, and I don’t want to let A or C down. Also, I rent, and my landlord would need to approve a change to what’s kept there—I haven’t asked him. Starting this way is okay.

#1 — I need the trailer for hauling on my home project in the next few weeks. It matters because the project needs it soon, and A also wants to use it soon.

#2 — “Neither of us is backing down” doesn’t quite fit. I don’t want my need dismissed or to be expected to wait until A is done; my project needs the trailer soon.

#3 — I don’t want B put in the middle or expected to settle this for us. The trailer is on B’s pad, so our plan affects B.

I have no other concern to add. Working with A means I want to keep this practical, but I can be candid. I have no discomfort with starting this way.

I want to use the trailer for my weekend trips in the next few weeks. What matters is having the freedom to make my own plans, and settling this soon because the trips are coming up. “Freedom to make my own plans” fits as my NCE. No discomfort with starting this way.

#4–#6 fit. Being in the middle is a separate concern: I don’t want to carry the responsibility for choosing between A and C; I want to keep things comfortable with both of them. Not having asked my landlord is mostly context, though I’d want to feel secure about my rental arrangement before raising a change. I am holding back a little because I don’t want to seem ungrateful, but I do need the space. No discomfort with starting this way.

#1 — Yes, “having the needs of my home project taken seriously” fits.

#2 — Yes, the revised concern fits, and “being treated as someone whose needs count alongside A’s” fits.

#3 — Yes, “B being treated as a neighbor with her own needs and choices” fits.

A wanting it soon is context for #1, not a separate concern. Working with A doesn’t make it harder for me to be candid; that’s not a separate concern. I’m not holding back, and I have no discomfort with the list.

I want the trailer in the next few weeks because my trips are coming up and I want freedom to make my own plans. “Neither of us is backing down” doesn’t fit me; I want to use it soon, but I’m willing to talk it through. I don’t want B stuck in the middle, since the trailer is at B’s place. No other concern or discomfort. Also, I already confirmed “freedom to make my own plans” as my NCE.

#9 fits. #10 concern fits, and the NCE fits. #11 fits, and “feeling secure about my housing situation” fits. I don’t think there’s anything else to add right now. I’m still a little unsure my needs will matter, but I appreciate you asking.

#7 still fits: “freedom to make my own plans.” That also covers #8; please use the same NCE. “Neither of us is backing down” still doesn’t fit. I don’t want B stuck in the middle, but I don’t know whether landlord approval is needed. No other concern or discomfort, and I’m not holding back.

It matters because I’d like to feel heard and comfortable with whatever happens, rather than agree while still uneasy. “Knowing my needs count in this conversation” fits. I’m not ready to treat everything as settled yet; please slow down and check in again. No discomfort with the pause.

#8: “Freedom to make my own plans” fits. #12: I’m willing to talk things through; it matters because I want us to work this out, not get stuck in a standoff. The proposed NCE fits. #13: I don’t want B put in the middle because the trailer is at her home and she has her own needs and choices. That NCE fits too. I’m not holding back, and I have no discomfort with the list or pause.

#16 wording fits. It matters that I feel heard and comfortable before agreeing, especially since I haven’t asked my landlord. I’m not ready to treat things as settled. Option 3 is closest, but I can’t say yes to it as a plan yet. I’d still like the trailer out of my way, and I’m not sure the list fully reflects that. I’m holding back a little, though I appreciate you checking.
